newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi continues price rally in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi continues price rally in Beirut.

text.p: Banque Audi rose on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Monday and dealers said strong demand would guarantee a continued price surge for the shining share.
Demand for Solidere A shares rose above last week's high levels with 139,600 shares changing hands compared with daily turnover of 40-50,000 in previous weeks and 80-100,000 last week.

Banque Audi closed at $18.125 from $18 -- the price at which they had traded throughout most of last week. The share had begun trading at $15 on January 20. A total of 30,000 shares changed hands against Friday's 27,850.
"Why should the share stop rising? As long as there is demand nothing will stop the rise," a dealer said.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce, the other listed bank, was unchanged at $12.875 on reduced turnover of 3,500 shares from 19,921 on Friday.
Solidere shares were steady on the market.

A one-week rise of Solidere's Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) which reached $12.8 on Friday from $11.05 a week earlier did not affect the Beirut price of the shares which traded at a low of $10.25 throughout last week.
On Monday, the GDRs slipped slightly to $12.65 as Solidere A shares held steady at $10.25. B shares were also unchanged at $10.75.
Dealers said the A shares -- distributed to former holders of property rights in central Beirut -- were trading at even lower prices on the grey market.

"Many new A share holders want to realise their cash so they go off the market and sell at discounted prices. I know the share has been trading on the grey market at between $8 and $8.5," a dealer said.
"There is oversupply on the official market. If A share holders place orders at $10.25, they know they might have to wait for one or two months before their order can be executed," the dealer added.
Total turnover was 198,898 shares for a value of $2,295,083 against 174,390 shares for a value of $2,062,680 on Friday.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Blancs, Ciments Libanais, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The BLOM stock index rose 0.02 percent to 896.74 and the LISPI rose 0.07 percent to 81.94.
